doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Saxophone, clarinet and Peabody
summary: Tommy's first instrument was saxophone; Peabody required clarinet, before his Air Force service. They joke about clarinet fingering.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Was saxophone your first instrument?
It was, yeah. Yeah, it was. I lusted after the saxophone, I really did. It was grand thing.
Well after you got over to — did you go to Peabody before you were in the Air Force or after?
Well let me think. It was before, yeah.
You were in the Air Force first, and then went to—
No I went to Peabody and then the Air Force.
Because he was in the Airmen of Note, the Air Force Band, which is still going.
Yeah. Better than ever.
And Peabody had saxophone?
No, saxophone was not accepted.
I kind of wondered.
The clarinet he had to play.
I had to study clarinet and they did me a big favor by making me do that.
Yeah, because that’s a hard instrument to learn the other way after you do the saxophone it seems like.
Yeah, well saxophone comes easy see? I mean you know it’s just up and down. Like Ernie Watts says, “The notes go up, the notes go down.”
It’s just like a piano. One is right next to the other one.
Yeah and you push the key and it’s the octave higher. With the clarinet you push the key, it’s a twelfth higher.
It goes an octave and a—
And a fifth. Very confusing.
Oh so if you’re playing C on a clarinet and you push the octave key, you’re going to get G then right?
Yeah.
Yeah. And when you’re used to the saxophone, see, that’s.
I’m getting educated on reeds and woodwinds right here.
That’s why clarinet players are crazy.

Why are you playing that when you could play a sax? I don’t understand. What was your first like memorable playing experience, either big band or combo or what you would consider to be your real start. I know you did Kai Winding.
